accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a simply connected open subset of R^n with the following two-convexity property: whenever three faces of a Euclidean 3-simplex Δ lie in Ω, the whole simplex Δ lies in Ω. Is every connected component of the intersection of Ω with an arbitrary 2-dimensional affine plane necessarily simply connected?

evidence.quote: Let Ω be a simply connected open set in R^n. Assume that Ω is two-convex; that is, if 3 faces of a 3-simplex △ lie in Ω, then △ ⊂ Ω. Is it true that any component of the intersection of Ω with any 2-plane is simply connected?

accepted.question_text: For n >= 1, let B_n denote the metric completion of the universal metric covering of the configuration space W_n = {(z_1, ..., z_n) in C^n : z_i != z_j for i != j}, equivalently the universal covering of C^n infinitely branching along the hyperplanes z_i = z_j, equipped with the lifted length metric. Is B_n a CAT(0) space for every n?

evidence.quote: Let us define braid space B_n as the universal covering of C_n infinitely branching along the complex hyperplanes z_i = z_j for i != j. We suppose that C_n is equipped with the canonical Euclidean metric, and B_n is equipped with lifted length metric.
In other words, if W_n denotes the complement of complex hyperplanes z_i = z_j in C_n, then the braid space B_n is the completion of the universal metric covering of W_n.
Is it true that B_n is CAT(0) for any n?

accepted.question_text: Suppose R is a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold that is isometric to a quotient of Hilbert space by a group of isometries, or more generally is the target of a Riemannian submersion from Hilbert space. Must R be isometric to a biquotient, meaning a quotient G//H of a compact Lie group G with a bi-invariant metric by a group of isometries?

evidence.quote: Suppose R is a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold that is isometric to a quotient of the Hilbert space by a group of isometries (or, more generally, R is the target of a Riemannian submersion from the Hilbert space). Is it true that R is isometric to a biquotient? That is, is it true that R is a quotient of a compact Lie group G with a bi-invariant metric by a group of isometries?

accepted.question_text: Which Riemannian metrics on the sphere S^n arise as metrics isometric to smooth nested convex surfaces, meaning an iterated chain of complete smooth convex hypersurfaces each embedded as a convex hypersurface inside the next one in some Euclidean space?

evidence.quote: Describe the Riemannian metrics on S^n that are isometric to smooth nested convex surfaces; that is, a complete smooth convex hypersurface in a complete smooth convex hypersurface in ... in a Euclidean space.

accepted.question_text: Let Γ act effectively, isometrically, and totally discontinuously on Euclidean space E^n. Prove that, up to conjugation in Γ, there are at most 2^n maximal finite subgroups of Γ.
accepted.context_brief: Maximal finite subgroups of Euclidean isometry groups

evidence.quote: Suppose that a group Γ acts effectively, isometrically, and totally discontinuously on Euclidean space E^n. Show that Γ contains at most 2^n maximal finite subgroups up to conjugation.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a compact connected subset of R^n, and let p and q be points of K. For every epsilon > 0, does there exist a curve gamma connecting p to q such that the total length of the part of gamma lying outside K is less than epsilon?
accepted.context_brief: Almost-inside paths in connected compact sets

evidence.quote: Let p and q be a pair of points in a compact connected subset K ⊂ R^n. Is it possible to connect p to q by a curve γ such that the length of γ \ K is arbitrarily small?

accepted.question_text: Let (S^3, g) be a Riemannian 3-sphere with sectional curvature at least 1, and suppose a closed geodesic gamma is the fixed-point set of an isometric involution of (S^3, g). Must the length of gamma be at most 2*pi?
accepted.context_brief: Geodesic fixed sets of involutions on S^3

evidence.quote: Suppose that a closed geodesic γ is the fixed-point set of an isometric involution of (S^3, g). Assume that the sectional curvature of g is at least 1. Is it true that length γ ⩽ 2·π?

accepted.question_text: Let d be the Fubini-Study metric on the complex projective plane CP^2. Does there exist a sequence of nonnegatively curved polyhedral metrics d_n on CP^2 that converges to d?

evidence.quote: A polyhedral metric on a compact manifold is a length metric such that, for some triangulation, each simplex is isometric to a simplex in Euclidean space. Such a metric is said to be nonnegatively curved if the total angle around each codimension-two simplex does not exceed 2·π; this is equivalent to nonnegative curvature in the sense of Alexandrov.
Let d be the Fubini–Study metric on the complex projective plane CP^2. Is it possible to find a sequence of nonnegatively curved polyhedral metrics d_n on CP^2 that converges to d?

accepted.question_text: Let O_3 be the octahedron graph. A metric space X satisfies O_3-comparison if every labeling of six points x, x', y, y', z, z' in X by the vertices of O_3 admits a model configuration in Hilbert space in which the three diagonal distances xx', yy', zz' do not decrease and all edge lengths do not increase. Does every geodesic CAT(0) space satisfy O_3-comparison?

evidence.quote: Suppose Γ is a graph with vertices v1, . . . , vn. We say that a metric space X meets the Γ-comparison if, for any set of points in X labeled by the vertices of Γ, there is a model configuration ṽ1, . . . , ṽn in the Hilbert space H such that if v_i is adjacent to v_j, then |ṽ_i − ṽ_j|_H ⩽ |v_i−v_j|_X, and otherwise, |ṽ_i−ṽ_j|_H ⩾ |v_i−v_j|_X.

Let us denote by O_3 the graph of the octahedron. For the labeling shown on the diagram, O_3-comparison means that any six-point configuration x, x′, y, y′, z, z′ ∈ X can be mapped to H so that the diagonals xx′, yy′, and zz′ do not get shorter and the edges do not get longer.
Is it true that O_3-comparison holds in any geodesic CAT(0) space?

accepted.question_text: In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by elements of finite order?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by finite-order elements

evidence.quote: Consider the Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension. Does it admit a discrete cocompact isometric action generated by (a) elements of finite order?

accepted.question_text: In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by central symmetries?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by central symmetries

evidence.quote: Consider the Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension. Does it admit a discrete cocompact isometric action generated by (b) central symmetries?

accepted.question_text: In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by rotations around subspaces of codimension k?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by codimension-k rotations

evidence.quote: Consider the Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension. Does it admit a discrete cocompact isometric action generated by (c) rotations around subspaces of codimension k?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a round spherical disc of radius α < π/2 on the unit sphere S^2, and let Ω′ be a convex domain in S^2 with the same area as Ω. Show that there exists a bi-Lipschitz map from Ω′ to the Euclidean plane whose Lipschitz constants are 1 and α/sin(α), that is, a (1, α/sin(α))-bi-Lipschitz map.

evidence.quote: Let Ω be a round disc of radius α < π/2 on the unit sphere S^2, and let Ω′ be a convex domain in S^2 with the same area as Ω. Show that there is a (1, α/sin α)-bi-Lipschitz map from Ω′ to the plane.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complete length CAT(0) space, not assumed locally compact, and let K be a compact subset of X. Is the closed convex hull of K, meaning the intersection of all closed convex subsets of X that contain K, necessarily compact?
accepted.context_brief: Compactness of convex hulls in CAT(0)

evidence.quote: Let X be a geodesic metric space. Recall that, a set C ⊂ X is called convex if, for any two points x, y ∈ C, every geodesic from x to y lies in C. The closed convex hull of a subset K ⊂ X is defined as the intersection of all closed convex sets containing K.
Let K be a compact subset in a complete length CAT(0) space X. Is it true that the closed convex hull of K is compact?

accepted.question_text: Let T be the 2-dimensional torus. A homeomorphism h: T -> T is called simple if it is supported on an embedded open disc, and the disc norm of h is the least number of simple homeomorphisms whose composition equals h. Do there exist homeomorphisms of T with arbitrarily large disc norm?

evidence.quote: A homeomorphism h: T → T is called simple if it is supported on an embedded open disc; that is, there is an embedded open disc Δ ⊂ T such that h is the identity outside of Δ.
The disc norm of a homeomorphism h: T → T is defined as the least number of simple homeomorphisms h1, . . . , hn such that h = h1 ◦ · · · ◦ hn.
Is there a homeomorphism of the 2-dimensional torus with arbitrarily large disc norm?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an embedding of the closed 4-ball D^4 into S^2 x R^2 such that the projection map from D^4 to S^2 induced by the first factor is open?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to construct an embedding D^4 → S^2 × R^2 such that the projection D^4 → S^2 is an open map?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature. Is it true that, with probability 1, a random geodesic in M eventually enters the subset where the curvature is strictly negative?

evidence.quote: Let M be a surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature. Show that, with probability 1, a random geodesic in M runs into the set of negative curvature.

accepted.question_text: Let (M, g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold, let p be a point of M, and let h be the pullback of g to the tangent space T_pM along the exponential map exp_p: T_pM -> M, allowing h to degenerate where exp_p fails to be regular. Does the possibly degenerate tensor h determine the pointed manifold (M, g, p) uniquely up to isometry?
accepted.context_brief: Ambrose problem for exponential pullback metrics

evidence.quote: Let (M, g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold, and let p ∈ M. Denote by h the pullback of the metric tensor g to the tangent space T_pM along the exponential map exp_p: T_pM → M; in general, h might degenerate at some points. Does h define the manifold (M, g) and the point p up to isometry?

accepted.question_text: Call a body V in R^3 an optical fiber if it is bounded by two plane figures F1 and F2 together with a smooth tube Σ, and every light ray entering V through one end and reflecting perfectly on the interior walls exits through the other end with probability 1, while every light ray starting inside V exits through one of the ends with probability 1. Must every such optical fiber admit a slicing into plane figures that meet the walls at right angles?

evidence.quote: Suppose that V is a body in R^3 bounded by two plane figures F1 and F2 (the ends) and a smooth surface Σ (a tube). Suppose that a light ray entering V thru one end and bouncing with perfect reflection from the interior walls of Σ will emerge from the other end with probability 1; moreover, a light ray that emerges from the interior of V, after bouncing, emerges from one of the ends with probability 1. In this case, we say that V is an optical fiber.
Is it always possible to slice an optical fiber into plane figures that meet the walls at right angles?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an optical fiber in R^3, in the sense of a reflective tube body with the almost-sure entrance and exit property described above, whose two planar ends are not congruent to each other?

evidence.quote: Suppose that V is a body in R^3 bounded by two plane figures F1 and F2 (the ends) and a smooth surface Σ (a tube). Suppose that a light ray entering V thru one end and bouncing with perfect reflection from the interior walls of Σ will emerge from the other end with probability 1; moreover, a light ray that emerges from the interior of V, after bouncing, emerges from one of the ends with probability 1. In this case, we say that V is an optical fiber.
In particular, Is there an optical fiber with noncongruent ends?

accepted.question_text: For each dimension n, does there exist a positive constant epsilon_n such that every open subset of R^n with volume at most epsilon_n admits an embedding into the unit ball that increases the lengths of all curves, equivalently a length-increasing embedding?

evidence.quote: Show that there is ε_n > 0 such that any open set in R^n with volume at most ε_n admits a length-increasing embedding into a unit ball.
